questions.q: What did Black Beauty's first master say when he left?
choices: "Good-by, Darkie; be a good horse, and always do your best."
"I will come and buy you back when I can, Darkie."
"Never trust a new master until he has earned it."
"Mind your manners, Darkie, and watch out for Ginger."
questions.evidence: be a good horse, and always do your best

questions.q: Why was the first stall called a "loose box"?
choices: The horse in it was not tied up but left loose
Its gate was broken and swung loose on its hinges
It was where the loose hay for the horses was kept
Its old wooden boards had worked loose over time
questions.evidence: because the horse that was put into it was not tied up, but left loose

choices: A little fat gray pony with a thick mane and tail
A tall chestnut mare with a long, handsome neck
A big black cart-horse with heavy, hairy feet
A thin brown racehorse with one white stocking

questions.q: What did Merrylegs say he did not like in a neighbor?
choices: A horse that bites
A horse that snores all night
A horse that eats too much hay
A horse that kicks at the stall
questions.evidence: I do not like any one next door who bites

questions.q: How did Ginger act toward Black Beauty when they first met?
choices: She was cross and said he had turned her out of her box
She was friendly and showed him around the whole stable
She ignored him and kept her head in the manger all day
She asked him to be her friend and share her loose box
questions.evidence: So it is you who have turned me out of my box

questions.q: Why were Miss Flora and Miss Jessie afraid to come into the stable?
choices: Ginger had bitten James and made his arm bleed
Merrylegs had kicked Miss Flora the week before
The stable was dark and full of strange noises
John Manly told them they must stay out of it
questions.evidence: she bit James in the arm and made it bleed

questions.q: What did Merrylegs think was the reason Ginger bit and snapped?
choices: She had been badly treated before she came
She was always hungry and never got enough oats
She was jealous of Merrylegs and the young ladies
She was very young and had not learned better yet
questions.evidence: she must have been very ill-used before she came here

questions.q: What did Merrylegs think of Birtwick Park as a home for horses?
choices: There was no better place for a horse in the whole country
It was too crowded, with too many horses for one stable
It was a nice place, but the grooms were often unkind
It was the worst place he had ever lived in his life
questions.evidence: there is not a better place for a horse all round the country than this
